problem: Zero-shot object navigation (ZSON) work follows single instructions to find generic object classes, with no language interaction or feedback and no handling of user-specific (personalized) objects.
motivation: Real household robots must ask questions, take user corrections, and identify objects by personal attributes such as owner names or purchase details. Feedback from the user can prevent endless wrong searches and let the robot adapt to a personal environment.
key_idea: An LLM acts as a sequential decision maker in a think-act-ask loop, calling perception, map, exploration, memory, control and dialogue modules through a unified python-function action space to find personalized goals while talking to the user.
insight: User feedback greatly raises success. In Table I, procedural feedback gives +21-26% SR over yes/no feedback, and landmark feedback also helps a lot. Balancing SR against SPL and SIT stays hard: ORION beats VLMap by over 10% SR but only about 2% SPL, and all agents are far below humans in interaction efficiency (SIT). Ablations show the semantic map matters most (SR 83.8 to 69.2 without it); memory helps little in a single zero-shot pass but reaches 91.5 SR on a second pass with accumulated memory.
method: Think-act-ask LLM controller: GPT-4 outputs JSON {Thought, Action}; the action is a python-style function call, and the function return is fed back as context until TALK is chosen and the user replies.
Semantic map: VLMap-style top-down map fusing LSeg features with CLIP; retrieve_map(obj_str) returns (id, distance, angle) contours.
Open-vocabulary detection: grounded-SAM projected to the 2D occupancy map; detect_object and double_check (move closer and re-detect).
Exploration: frontier-based exploration with an initial 360° spin, exposed as search_object.
Memory: positive and negative CLIP-feature maps M_pos and M_neg storing user-affirmed and denied descriptions; update_memory and retrieve_memory.
Control and interaction: Move/Rotate primitives, goto_point/goto_object (fast marching planner), and talk(content) for text dialogue with the user.
ZIPON benchmark: personalized goals with type/name/room/feedback dictionary, an LLM-based user simulator, four feedback types (corrective, descriptive, landmark, procedural), and SR/SPL/SIT metrics.

setting.backbone: GPT-4-8k-0613 (frozen) as controller; LSeg, CLIP ViT-B-32, grounded-SAM frozen; GPT-3.5-turbo as user simulator
setting.action_space: low-level TURN LEFT/RIGHT 15°, MOVE FORWARD 0.25 m, plus TALK; high-level goto_point/goto_object wrappers
setting.simulator: Habitat with HM3D v0.2; real TIAGo robot
setting.privileged: Semantic map is built beforehand from 14,159 collected RGB-D frames of the test scenes (pre-exploration for the map); the user simulator sees ground truth goal info.

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 randomly selected HM3D v0.2 val scenes, 117 goal objects, 5 runs; mixed-feedback
numbers.extra: mixed user feedback, I_max=5, success radius 1.5 m; semantic map built from pre-collected frames

numbers_note: Results are on the authors' own ZIPON benchmark, not a standard one. Table I has more feedback types, ablations are in Table II, and the real-robot no-interaction result is in Table III (SR 37.5).
results: ORION reaches 83.8 SR / 56.6 SPL / 53.5 SIT in the mixed-feedback setting, beating CoW (62.4), VLMap (71.8) and ConceptFusion (73.5) in SR. With no interaction its SR is only 28.2, and user feedback lifts it to 54.2-80.3. On the real robot, SR rises from 37.5 without interaction to 72.5 with landmark or procedural feedback.
limitations: Trade-off between SR and SPL/SIT remains: ORION's active exploration costs path efficiency and it relies heavily on interaction (humans reach 94-97 SR with much better SIT).

Evaluation is small (10 scenes, 117 goals in simulation; 20 objects in one real room) and uses an LLM-simulated user with a semantic map built in advance; real-world tests use a simplified topology map.
Does not handle image goals or multimodal user interaction; detection and low-level movement errors cause failures.
